explanations: There is none. Only one timer is pending at a time (pump returns early while this.timer is set), each start sets nextSlotAt = now + minIntervalMs before running the task, and the next timer waits until that slot, so call starts are spaced at least 200 ms apart (at most 5/s). The queue is capped at 50, so memory and wait time are bounded and overflow fails fast. task() is invoked inside run(), so a synchronous throw from task would escape, but here the task is an async function, which turns throws into rejections forwarded via then(resolve, reject); the finally guarantees pumping continues.

The first call starts on a 0 ms timer, and each start schedules the next no earlier than 200 ms later, so call n starts about (n-1) x 200 ms: the tenth at about 1.8 s. Pacing is on start times, not completion, so it does not wait for the 2 s timeout; nothing allows simultaneous starts.

run() fires task() and returns without awaiting it, and pump() is called in finally right away, so the executor limits the start rate, not concurrency. With 1.5 s per call and a start every 200 ms, about 7-8 overlap. It does not serialize or pause, and the abort timeout is 2 s, not 200 ms.

submit rejects with QueueFullError once 50 are waiting (one may already have been dequeued by the first timer, so the split is approximate). quote() catches QueueFullError and returns FALLBACK_QUOTE with estimated: true, so it is not rethrown. Queued requests are still served by the real API.
